Interceptor 

 
 Give your agent your browser, Mac, and iPhone. 
 

 
 Browser automation, computer use, and iPhone automation for AI agents.
 

 
 Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Claude Desktop, OpenClaw, OpenCode, and any agent that can run a shell command.
 

 
 Get started ·
 How it compares ·

 iPhone ·
 Record & replay ·

Interceptor reads GitHub stats, fills a Numbers sheet, and builds an on-screen overlay.

 

 30-second edited demo. The terminal is staged from real Interceptor output. 

Interceptor connects an AI agent or script to your signed-in browser, native apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and a physical iPhone. It combines structured UI reads and actions with access to page traffic, rich editors, app internals, and device state. The agent can inspect what happened after an action and use that evidence for its next step.

 Work you can build with Interceptor Tools available 
 --- --- 
 Research in your existing browser session Page text, tables, links, browser search, multiple contexts, and a source-ledger research workflow. 
 Edit a document, slide, or design and save the result Rich-editor scenes, canvas input, file uploads, and direct capture of page-produced export bytes. 
 Complete a native desktop task while you keep working Accessibility controls, background input, and capture of covered windows on macOS, Windows, and Linux; Apple Events on the Mac. 
 Operate an app on a real iPhone and inspect its state Element trees, taps, text entry, screenshots, process telemetry, and WebKit inspection. 
 Turn a demonstrated workflow into reusable commands Browser and Mac recording, event timelines, and replay-plan export. 

Use it from any agent that can run shell commands, or through its built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Interceptor does not require a model API key; your chosen agent or model may have its own subscription or API costs.

 What Interceptor adds

Many tools now let an agent use your signed-in Chrome, and several work on a Mac in the background. Interceptor does both, and adds what the tools in How it compares don't:

- Safari and Chromium in one CLI. Chrome, Brave, Edge, and Safari pages, with the same commands, in the profiles you already use.
- Your own iPhone. Drive the apps on a physical iPhone, not a simulator, over USB, Wi-Fi, or Tailscale away from home, including on cellular.
- Page traffic without a debugger. Read fetch, XHR, SSE, WebSocket, Beacon, and BroadcastChannel traffic through standard page APIs. The browser shows no debugging banner and needs no remote-debugging switch.
- Real editors, not screenshots. Read and change Google Docs, Slides, Sheets, and Canva through their scene graphs, and save the files they export.
- Admin work without showing the password. Vault secrets go by name into a web login, sudo , the macOS administrator prompt, or the iPhone passcode. The model never sees the value.
- One tool across browser, Mac, Windows, Linux, and iPhone, with any agent and any model. Work runs in the background so you keep using your computer. Behavior and exceptions.

It asks two questions. Press Enter for both to get everything:

1. Full or Browser only? Full (the default) is your browser plus desktop apps, and the iPhone on a Mac. Browser only is web pages.
2. Register the MCP server? Yes is the default. It lists the AI apps it found that don't have the server yet (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Claude Desktop) and turns every tool on.

It downloads the latest release from updates.hackervalley.media , checks its SHA-256 and the Hacker Valley Media signature, and installs it with no Installer wizard. Nothing installs if a check fails. It adds Interceptor's skills to every AI agent on your computer. A Mac asks for your password once. Run it again any time to update: it keeps your edition and leaves an existing MCP setup alone.

Options go after bash -s -- , for example curl -fsSL … bash -s -- --browser --no-mcp :

 Option Does 
 --- --- 
 --full , --browser Pick the edition instead of being asked. Full is the default. 
 --mcp , --no-mcp Register the MCP server in every AI app it finds, or skip it, instead of being asked ( --mcp=claude,codex for some). 
 --safari macOS: also install the Safari extension package. 
 --no-skills Skip adding the skills. 

On Windows, pass the same as parameters: & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm ))) -Browser -NoMcp .

"Every tool on" means the agent can also run the actions that are off by default, such as quitting apps, writing files, and running scripts in a page ( INTERCEPTOR MCP ALLOW=all,raw ). The agent still marks each of those calls as confirmed. For reading and clicking only, run interceptor mcp install afterward.

The last step is the browser extension. On a Mac, the Interceptor window opens by itself and walks you through it. On Windows, the Chrome Web Store page opens.

Want your AI agent to do it? Ask it to run the same command. With no terminal to answer, it takes the defaults: Full and the MCP server with every tool on. A Mac then opens the verified package in Installer for you to type your password.

install.html:
Install with one command

macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Hacker-Valley-Media/Interceptor/main/scripts/get-interceptor.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell):

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Hacker-Valley-Media/Interceptor/main/scripts/get-interceptor.ps1 | iex

It asks two questions. Press Enter for both to get everything:

  1. Full or Browser only? Full (the default) is your browser plus desktop apps, and the iPhone on a Mac. Browser only is web pages.
  2. Register the MCP server? Yes is the default. It lists the AI apps it found that don't have the server yet (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Claude Desktop) and turns every tool on.

It downloads the latest release from updates.hackervalley.media, checks its SHA-256 and the Hacker Valley Media signature, and installs it with no Installer wizard. Nothing installs if a check fails. It adds Interceptor's skills to every AI agent on your computer. A Mac asks for your password once. Run it again any time to update: it keeps your edition and leaves an existing MCP setup alone.

Options go after bash -s --, for example curl -fsSL … | bash -s -- --browser --no-mcp:

Option Does
--full, --browser Pick the edition instead of being asked. Full is the default.
--mcp, --no-mcp Register the MCP server in every AI app it finds, or skip it, instead of being asked (--mcp=claude,codex for some).
--safari macOS: also install the Safari extension package.
--no-skills Skip adding the skills.

On Windows, pass the same as parameters: & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm <url>))) -Browser -NoMcp.

"Every tool on" means the agent can also run the actions that are off by default, such as quitting apps, writing files, and running scripts in a page (INTERCEPTOR_MCP_ALLOW=all,raw). The agent still marks each of those calls as confirmed. For reading and clicking only, run interceptor mcp install afterward.

The last step is the browser extension. On a Mac, the Interceptor window opens by itself and walks you through it. On Windows, the Chrome Web Store page opens.

Want your AI agent to do it? Ask it to run the same command. With no terminal to answer, it takes the defaults: Full and the MCP server with every tool on. A Mac then opens the verified package in Installer for you to type your password.

Prefer to run each step yourself? On a Mac, the same install with Apple's own tools:

curl -fLo /tmp/Interceptor.pkg https://updates.hackervalley.media/latest/Interceptor-Full.pkg
spctl -a -vv -t install /tmp/Interceptor.pkg && sudo installer -pkg /tmp/Interceptor.pkg -target /
interceptor skills adopt

spctl is Apple's Gatekeeper check. It prints Notarized Developer ID and HACKER VALLEY MEDIA, LLC (TPWBZD35WW), and if the package is not signed and notarized, installer never runs. For the Browser edition, use Interceptor-Browser.pkg. Add interceptor mcp install --allow all,raw to register the MCP server with every tool on.

Download an installer

Each link below always gets the newest release. Start with Browser for web tasks, or Full for native apps and the iPhone. Every version is on Releases, and SHA256SUMS-ALL lists each file's SHA-256. The macOS packages are built for Apple silicon. On an Intel Mac, build from source (see Development and contributions).

Package Download What it enables
macOS Browser (Apple silicon, macOS 13+) Interceptor-Browser.pkg CLI, daemon, and browser extension files.
macOS Full (Apple silicon, macOS 15+) Interceptor-Full.pkg Browser package plus the native Mac bridge and iPhone tooling.
macOS Safari add-on (Apple silicon, macOS 14+) Interceptor-Safari.pkg Safari extension, installed after either core package.
Windows Browser x64 · ARM64 Browser automation on Windows 10 22H2+ or Windows 11 (x64); Windows 11 24H2+ (ARM64). Windows guide.
Windows Full x64 · ARM64 Browser automation plus native app control with interceptor desktop. Windows 10 22H2 x64 or Windows 11 24H2+ (x64/ARM64).
Linux Browser x64 · ARM64 Browser automation and install scripts.
Linux Full x64 · ARM64 Browser automation plus native app control with interceptor desktop.

The macOS release binaries target Apple silicon. On Windows and Linux, the Full packages add native app control through interceptor desktop; run interceptor desktop capabilities to see what works on that computer. iPhone setup requires a Mac.

macOS installation
  1. Install the Browser or Full .pkg. On a first install, the Interceptor window opens: it checks whether the extension is already in your browser, and if not, walks you through adding it from the Chrome Web Store, as an unpacked extension (with a step-by-step guide in the browser), or for Safari. Open it again any time with interceptor diagnose extension --welcome.
  2. In Chrome or Brave, install the Interceptor extension if the window did not already do it. The local runtime and browser extension are both required.
  3. For Safari, also install the Safari .pkg, open /Applications/InterceptorSafari.app once, then enable Interceptor and website access in Safari → Settings → Extensions. Safari requires your approval.
  4. With Full, grant the permissions needed by your task to interceptor-bridge. Run interceptor macos trust --walkthrough for guidance. Accessibility enables native UI control; screen, microphone, and app-automation access are needed for their respective features.

For an unpacked Chrome/Brave extension, enable Developer Mode on the browser's extensions page and load /Library/Application Support/Interceptor/extension/. Keep one copy per profile. Store and unpacked installations share an extension ID; store updates arrive after store review.

Windows and Linux

On Windows, run the installer for your PC (x64 or ARM64), install the browser extension, then open a new terminal. Chrome, Brave, and Edge can use the Chrome Web Store listing; Edge requires allowing extensions from other stores. The Windows guide also covers unpacked extensions, silent installation, updates, and removal.

On Linux, extract the archive for your machine (x64 or ARM64) and run this from its directory:

bash scripts/install.sh --browser-only --brave
# For Chrome, use --chrome instead of --brave.
./dist/interceptor open "https://example.com"

Follow the installer's extension-loading instructions. The archive includes compiled binaries, so a separate Bun installation is not needed for this release path.
